content.title: How old was Miley Cyrus in ‘Hannah Montana’?
content.text: EntertainmentUpdated: Mar. 24, 2026, 5:46 p.m.Published: Mar. 24, 2026, 5:45 p.m.Billy Ray Cyrus and Miley Cyrus in 2006.APMiley Cyrus is fully embracing her Disney Channel roots.Cyrus, now 33, spearheaded the “Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special,” which premiered on Disney+ and Hulu on Tuesday, March 24, 2026. “She willed it into existence,” Disney executive Charlie Andrews told Variety for a piece published ahead of the special’s premiere. “The thing she was adamant about is that this is for the fans. That has gone into literally every decision she has made.” Cyrus was just 13 years old when she filmed season 1 of “Hannah Montana.” The series, which premiered in March 2006, starred Cyrus as the titular pop star who had a double life as ordinary teenager Miley Stewart. By the time the show ended after four seasons and a feature film in 2011, Cyrus was 18. Cyrus went on to have a successful music career, releasing nine studio albums to date. In 2024, she won her first two Grammy awards, Record of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance, for her song “Flowers.” For all her continued success, Cyrus never forgets that it all started with “Hannah Montana.”“I think even Disney sometimes forgets the connection between me and Hannah,” she recently told Variety. “It’s not just a TV show. I see daily how important Hannah is to people. When I travel, people bring me ‘Hannah’ merch. They ask, ‘Are you ever going to do another season?’” Several of Cyrus’s former “Hannah Montana” costars attended the premiere of the anniversary special, including Jason Earles (Jackson Stewart) and Moisés Arias (Rico Suave). Aside from Cyrus’s dad, Billy Ray Cyrus, Earles was the oldest member of the “Hannah Montana” cast, while Arias was the youngest. How old was Jason Earles in ‘Hannah Montana’?Jason Earles in 2008.ASSOCIATED PRESSWhile Cyrus was barely a teenager when “Hannah Montana” premiered, Earles was 28. He lied and told casting directors he was 18 years old to land the role of 16-year-old Jackson. “I was desperately afraid that I was going to be fired and recast because I had a big secret,” Earles, now 48, said during the first episode of “Best of Both Our Worlds: The Official, Unofficial Hannah Montana Podcast,” which launched earlier this month. Earles noted that network executives didn’t learn his real age “until halfway through the first season.” He was 33 by the time “Hannah Montana” ended.
